tasks.short: Resolve staff problems and explain policy

steps.what: Check the relevant company policy and factual personnel context
Confer with staff to resolve performance problems and discuss policies
Write the necessary personnel case note and agreed actions

tasks.design: Use current-policy links in {DOCS} and the existing personnel-case form in {HCM}. The supervisor keeps the discussion human and writes its necessary case note separately, reusing identity and action headings without automating personnel judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy searching and repeated case headings take time around the discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Native policy links and personnel forms may reduce those clerical operations.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting accounts and sensitive circumstances require fair listening.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor can distinguish a support need from misconduct and adapt the conversation.
tasks.altitude: A small clerical saving leaves more attention for the employee's account.

reach.learn: Policy interpretation and confidential case notes

evidence.claim: Native policy links and structured case headings can reduce lookup and repeated entry without replacing the discussion.

assumptions: Boundary includes preparation, the staff conversation and its real personnel case note. Casual policy questions that require no record do not acquire a new record; confirm the actual case mix before using the estimate.

The policy owner produces the current policy and the supervisor produces the staff account, agreed action, responsible person and date in s2-s3. Retained12 lookup hours and11.25 note-writing hours include source checking and capture. Missing facts remain explicit and are resolved manually.
Try native links and forms before code. An ordinary author save has no self-approval gate and earns no saving.
No transcript, staff score, automated escalation send or extra approval is introduced.
unknowns: Which current personnel discussions require a case note
research_questions: Can native headings remove repeat entry without turning an employee account into unsupported conclusions?

tasks.short: Evaluate performance and recommend personnel actions

steps.what: Collect and check employee performance evidence
Discuss performance evidence and the employee's explanation
Evaluate performance and choose a justified personnel recommendation
Write the evaluation and reasoned recommendation
Send the final recommendation to the personnel decision maker

tasks.design: Use native inspection-record links from the {OTHER} cleaning-operations system and a structured evaluation form in {HCM}. The supervisor interprets the evidence, writes the reasons and separately sends the final recommendation; no model ranks employees or chooses a personnel action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence and review headings are copied across records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native links and existing review forms may reduce source navigation and repeated factual entry.
tasks.still_hard: The same inspection result can reflect workload, equipment, training or individual conduct.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor tests explanations and judges proportional action.
tasks.altitude: Less evidence copying leaves more time to assess context fairly; decision rights do not expand.

reach.learn: Comparable evidence and fair personnel process

evidence.claim: FacilityApps supports inspection forms, photographic evidence and reports; this supports record availability, not employee scoring or a local time estimate.

OTHER is the cleaning-operations system. Test native links and review forms before code; access must remain limited to the review purpose.

steps.what: Review service complaints, inspection findings and current work arrangements
Observe the work and discuss practical constraints with cleaning staff
Choose changes that could improve service and operational efficiency
Write the improvement proposal and its supporting evidence
Present the final recommendation to the service manager

tasks.design: Use existing service and quality views in the {OTHER} cleaning-operations system and a short proposal template in {DOCS}. These reduce navigation and repeated headings, while observation, choosing the change, writing its local reasoning and presenting it remain the supervisor's work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service findings are scattered and proposals repeat the same structure.
tasks.enabler_now: Native quality views and a reusable proposal layout can remove those particular operations.
tasks.still_hard: A change that looks efficient may shift work or reduce service quality elsewhere.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor tests whether the change is workable for the people doing the cleaning.

ambition.what: Consider a small service improvement at each routine service review

tasks.altitude: More attention can go to testing practical improvements instead of assembling the proposal.

tasks.short: Screen applicants and hire cleaning staff

steps.what: Screen job applicants against the actual vacancy requirements
Interview applicants about relevant work and availability
Write the factual interview evaluation
Choose whom to hire within existing authority
Write and check the offer using the agreed employment terms
Send the final offer to the chosen applicant
Enter the accepted hire and start details in the employee record

tasks.design: Use native applicant views and evaluation fields in {ATS}, a checked offer template in {DOCS}, and the existing starter form in {HCM}. The supervisor screens, interviews and chooses the hire, writes the evaluation separately, sends the exact offer and records an accepted hire in its later phase.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applicant facts, evaluation headings and offer terms are repeatedly copied.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms and offer layouts can reduce field navigation and retyping without candidate ranking.
tasks.still_hard: Relevant experience, availability and fair comparisons need human assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor can explore an unclear answer and judge the candidate against actual work needs.
tasks.altitude: Less hiring paperwork leaves more attention for a fair interview; hiring authority is unchanged.

reach.role: First-Line Supervisors of Landscaping, Lawn Service, and Groundskeeping Workers
reach.learn: Job-related criteria and accurate offer terms

evidence.claim: Native applicant views, evaluation forms and offer templates can reduce repetitive clerical work; no automated selection or measured saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary includes screening, interview, real evaluation writing, hiring choice, offer preparation and send, then accepted-hire entry. Recruiting administration retains any existing invitation handling; no invitation automation or saving is introduced.

Applicants produce application facts; the supervisor verifies requirements in s1 and produces evidence in s2-s3. Retained17 screening hours and8 evaluation-writing hours include capture and checking. Missing facts remain questions for the interview, never inferred scores.

The supervisor produces candidate identity, role, pay, hours and start date in s5 from the decision and agreed terms; its9 retained hours include checking. The applicant supplies acceptance and starter details later; s7 retains4 hours for their capture and verification. Missing or conflicting terms use manual writing.
Test native views, forms and templates before code. No same-system author save has an approval stage or a saving claim. The offer send has its own exact-version gate, with all5 send hours retained.
No additional approval hierarchy, candidate scoring model or automated hiring commit is introduced.
unknowns: Supervisor versus recruiting-admin ownership of offer and starter forms
research_questions: How much clerical time remains after native field reuse and actual term checking?
